drafts.body:

drafts.title: [R10-SCORES] Plan scores read 0 for no evidence, the house score misreads a two-zone house, and scores contradict other tabs
drafts.body:
Owner-reported (tvofi). The owner's report, as the orchestrator's plan recorded it:

> - **R10-SCORES: the plan scores (tvofi, 2026-10-14).** Read from `coordinator._scores_view` and `_close_score_day` at main 554e2ecfa:
>   1. **The heat-pump score reads 0 with too little COP data.** `machine` is `None` when no COP baseline has `COP_BASELINE_MIN_SAMPLES`, so the 0 comes from the sensor or card turning "no evidence" into 0. It must render "–" / N/A with a reason. Every score shares one rule: None means no evidence, and it is never 0.
>   2. **The house score reads 0 on an averagely insulated house with new windows.** It is not a diff against the initial setpoint. It is the time constant τ = room_thermal_mass / (heat_loss_coefficient × learned `house_heat_loss_scale`), mapped from 20–100 h to 0–100 and clipped. Three causes are suspected:
>      - **(a)** The learned scale has drifted ×2.6 in autumn (see the R10-RESEED drift lead: solar and other confounds), which drives τ under 20 h.
>      - **(b)** For two zones, τ ignores the lower-floor learned ratio and zone masses.
>      - **(c)** The 20/80 h band is an absolute, uncalibrated heuristic, and the configured thermal mass may be the default.
> 
>      Measure τ on tvofi's bundle stores, and fix the envelope grade to use whole-house UA (both zones) and its confidence. Show "–" while the heat-loss learner is still converging or drifting. Once fixed, the house-heat-loss result must agree with the Health tab's figure.
>   3. **One message everywhere.** The scores must not contradict the Savings, Advisor and Health insights: the same evidence, the same thresholds and the same "not enough data" state. Use one view model, and add a consistency test that walks every card surface for each score input.
> 
>   Ordering: `after` R10-RATIO-SITES and R10-SAV-BASELINE (shared inputs), and before the card groups. The card rendering joins R10-UX-HEALTH.

**Evidence.** Owner report 2026-10-14, read from the coordinator's score view at main 554e2ecfa. Folds ARCH2-s5 C3.

**Roster group.** `R10-SCORES` in `dev/programme/rosters/wave-r10-groups.json` (lane UI, wave 17, size L, after: R10-ADVISOR, R10-RATIO-SITES). The group's brief carries the fix shape, the null control and the forward-carried constraints.

drafts.title: [R10-HEAT-METER] Add a delivered-heat energy input; measured COP and the house learner's delivered heat, split by mode
drafts.body:
Owner-reported (tvofi). The owner's report, as the orchestrator's plan recorded it:

> ### R10-HEAT-METER (tvofi asked 2026-10-15; added as a group)
> - Main has no delivered-heat energy input. The only heat-output path is CONF_FLOW_METER_ENTITY (mass flow × supply–return ΔT, `flow_meter.read_heat_output_kw`), and it is used ONLY when there is no power and no frequency signal. So an install with a power meter never measures heat.
> - tvofi has a delivered-heat entity (kWh, cumulative). The group:
>   - adds an optional `heat_energy_entity` (total_increasing kWh);
>   - reads Δheat over each interval;
>   - makes measured COP = Δheat/Δelectric the COP sample whenever both meters exist. That replaces "modelled COP × asked/drawn" and removes the draw-follows-plan assumption (study Q2/L3).
>   - Δheat also gives the house learner a true delivered-heat input (fixes the L1 delivery shortfall at the root).
> - Guards: counter resets and rollover; interval alignment between the two meters (their update cadences differ); a defrost or DHW share split (DHW heat must not feed the space learner; DHW intervals get their own COP bin); a minimum Δ so quantisation does not dominate.
> - Tests: synthetic plant with a known COP gives an exact fold; null control with heat = COP×elec reproduces the model; a planted reset is refused.
> - Ordering: before R10-COP-GATE, which then only handles installs without a heat meter, and with G-ID-3. Config-flow/strings changes join R10-UX-SETUP's deep-link work.
> 2. R10-HEAT-METER: no entity is added yet. The meter will count heating AND DHW, so the group must split delivered heat and electric power into DHW and space using the heat pump mode entity, per interval, by the time share in each mode. The tests owe a mixed-mode interval, and the mode entity must be required when the heat meter is configured, with a refusal if it is missing. Same split for electric power.

**Evidence.** Owner request 2026-10-15 and the owner's answer the same day (heating plus hot water; split by the mode entity; mode entity required).

**Roster group.** `R10-HEAT-METER` in `dev/programme/rosters/wave-r10-groups.json` (lane LR, wave 23, size XL, after: R10-LEARNER-ETA, R10-INPUT-STALENESS, R10-UX-SETUP, R10-RATIO-ANCHOR). The group's brief carries the fix shape, the null control and the forward-carried constraints.

drafts.title: [R10-UX-HEALTH] Health tab: one label source, responsive list, sticky-header clip, Show link, learner state, direct diagnostics download
drafts.body:
Owner-reported (tvofi). The owner's report, as the orchestrator's plan recorded it:

> - **R10-UX-HEALTH: Health tab input list.** From tvofi's screenshot of 2026-10-14:
>   1. **Mixed casing.** "Lower floor", "Heat pump power", "Hot-water tank" and "Buffer tank" sit next to "wood tank top", "heat pump supply temp", "heat pump mode" and "heat pump defrost". The lowercase rows look like the user's own entity friendly names passed through raw, while the others are the integration's role labels. Every row shows the integration's translated role label, with the entity name as secondary text if it is shown at all. The rule is a single label source, and a check fails any input row whose label does not come from `strings.json`.
>   2. **Half-width list.** The list fills only the left half on a wide screen, and the right half is empty. Use a responsive grid of 2 columns, or the full width.
>   3. **Clipping under the sticky header.** The first row ("Outdoor temperature") is clipped under the header when scrolled.
> 
>   4. **"Show" opens the wrong page.** The checklist row "Some insight sensors are off by default" opens only the integration's front page. It must land on exactly the disabled entities: HA's entity table, filtered to this config entry with disabled entities shown.
>   5. **Contradictory efficiency row.** It says "Not enough running history to watch yet" next to a confident "Normal (COP scale 1.00)". When the learner lacks history, the value must read as not-yet-learned rather than "Normal".
>   6. **Internal-gains peak at 03:00.** The card says "add up to 0.4 kW around 03:00", which is physically odd for people and cooking. This goes as a lead to the D2 estimator seat (M5) and the D15 live-bundle seat. It becomes a fix only if a finder measures it as a learner artefact.
> 
>   7. **"Download diagnostics" downloads nothing.** The button only explains how to find the menu. It should download the file directly, through HA's authenticated diagnostics endpoint for this config entry, and fall back to the integration page if the fetch is refused.

**Evidence.** Owner screenshot 2026-10-14. Item 6 (internal gains at 03:00) is a lead, not owed; item 8 (RESEED) was a study that returned NO-GO.

**Roster group.** `R10-UX-HEALTH` in `dev/programme/rosters/wave-r10-groups.json` (lane UI, wave 25, size L, after: R10-SCORES, R10-COP-GATE, R10-HEAT-METER). The group's brief carries the fix shape, the null control and the forward-carried constraints.

drafts.title: [R10-PREPR-CAP] The prepr cap of 4 is advisory; 10 concurrent prepr runs drove load1 to 168 on 8 cores
drafts.body:
Instrument defect found while running round 10, as recorded:

> **Lead for D13/D11: R10-PREPR-CAP.**
> - What happened: the prepr cap of 4 is only advisory. At 22:57 the tick read 10 prepr runs, each spawning a nested chain of `--self-test` runs, and load1 reached 168 on 8 cores.
